verses.text: When David was old and had lived a long life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
He brought together all Israel's leaders, along with the priests and Levites.
The Levite men who were thirty years old and up were counted one by one. There were thirty-eight thousand of them.
David said, "Twenty-four thousand of these men will oversee the work at the LORD's house, and six thousand will serve as officers and judges.
Four thousand will guard the doors, and four thousand will praise the LORD with the instruments I made for that purpose."
David organized them into groups by their descent from Levi's sons Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The Gershonite lines were Ladan and Shimei.
Ladan had three sons: Jehiel, who was the head, Zetham, and Joel.
Shimei had three sons: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. These were the heads of Ladan's families.
Shimei had four sons: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah.
Jahath was the head, and Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah had few sons, so their families were counted together as one household.
Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his sons were set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, burn incense before the LORD, serve him, and pronounce blessings in his name.
The sons of Moses, the man of God, were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
Moses' sons were Gershom and Eliezer.
Shebuel was the head of Gershom's family.
Eliezer's son Rehabiah was the head. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah had many sons.
Shelomith was the head of Izhar's family.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah, who was the head, then Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
Uzziel's sons were Micah, who was the head, and Isshiah, who was second.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died leaving daughters and no sons. Their relatives, the sons of Kish, married them.
Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
These were Levi's descendants by family, including the heads of the families. The men twenty years old and up who worked in the service of the LORD's house were listed and counted by name.
David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given his people rest, and he lives in Jerusalem forever.
So the Levites no longer have to carry the tabernacle or any of the equipment used in its service."
Under David's final instructions, Levi's descendants were counted from twenty years old and up.
Their job was to help Aaron's descendants serve at the LORD's house. They looked after the courtyards and rooms, purified all the sacred things, and did the work needed at God's house.
They also looked after the bread set before God, the fine flour for grain offerings, the unleavened wafers, the offerings baked in pans or prepared by soaking, and every measure of quantity and size.
Each morning and evening they were to stand and thank and praise the LORD.
They were also to present the burnt offerings to the LORD on Sabbaths, at new moons, and at the appointed festivals, regularly offering the prescribed number before him.
They were to carry out their duties for the Tent of Meeting and the holy place and help their fellow Levites, Aaron's descendants, in serving at the LORD's house.
